bugs.title: Ducking default flip makes unit tests fire real busctl --user calls against the live desktop session (test pollution + operator media can be paused)
bugs.description: P1.M2.T4.S1 flipped the shipped default audio.duck_mode from "off" to "mpris" (voice_typing/config.py, config.toml:61), but the many tests that construct a default-config VoiceTypingDaemon and call _arm() were not made hermetic. daemon.py:1022-1023 builds a REAL AsyncDucker(AudioDucker(MprisBusctlBackend)) whenever duck_mode != "off", and _arm() (daemon.py:1804) dispatches _duck_engage(), so every such test spawns a leaked 'vt-ducking' daemon worker that runs /usr/bin/busctl --user against the operator's LIVE session bus (/run/user/1000/bus). Two consequences: (1) CROSS-FILE TEST POLLUTION — the leaked worker's subprocess.run calls (kwargs {'timeout': 1.0, 'check': False, 'stdout': PIPE, 'stderr': DEVNULL} from ducking_mpris.py:_run) land inside later tests' monkeypatched subprocess.run recorders, producing order-dependent failures (tests/test_typing_backends.py::test_wtype_passes_check_true and test_wtype_invokes_exact_argv fail whenever an arming key_listener test precedes them); (2) LIVE-SIDE EFFECT — the engage path enumerates MPRIS players and PAUSES every Playing+CanPause one (ducking_mpris.py:_engage_mpris), with no resume because the test daemons never disarm; on a desktop with music/video playing, running the unit suite pauses the operator's media. This violates PRD §4.2sexies R.7's law that automation MUST NOT exercise the live desktop. Verified live in this session: constructing a default-config daemon and calling _arm() produced real calls 'busctl --user call org.freedesktop.DBus ... ListNames' and 'busctl --user get-property org.mpris.MediaPlayer2.brave.instance479674 ... PlaybackStatus' (the operator's real Brave browser endpoint). Affected arming tests include tests/test_key_listener.py:459 (test_zero_keyboard_warning_fires_once_at_first_arm) and :477 (test_no_warning_when_keyboards_watched), plus default-config arm sites in tests/test_bulk_dispatch.py, tests/test_daemon.py, tests/test_voicectl.py, tests/test_session_recovery.py, tests/test_context_prompt_refresh.py, tests/test_bulk_context_prompt.py, tests/test_ime_manager.py (none set duck_mode or inject a ducker; only test_no_warning_before_listener_started at tests/test_key_listener.py:492-509 explicitly sets duck_mode="off", with a comment acknowledging the noise).
bugs.reproduction: Deterministic (3/3 runs): cd /home/dustin/projects/voice-typing && timeout 300 .venv/bin/pytest tests/test_key_listener.py::test_zero_keyboard_warning_fires_once_at_first_arm tests/test_typing_backends.py -q → 1 failed: tests/test_typing_backends.py::test_wtype_passes_check_true (recorder.calls[0] kwargs are the leaked busctl call's {'timeout': 1.0, 'check': False, ...} instead of wtype's check=True). Same failure occurs with the full files tests/test_key_listener.py + tests/test_typing_backends.py (3/3), and intermittently (2/5) with the 8-file batch tests/{test_control_socket,test_key_listener,test_typing_backends,test_textproc,test_prompt_engine,test_context_prompt_refresh,test_systemd_unit,test_ydotoold_client}.py. Live-session proof: python snippet constructing VoiceTypingConfig() (default duck_mode='mpris') + VoiceTypingDaemon(...)._arm(), sleep 2.5s with a subprocess.run spy → 2 real /usr/bin/busctl --user calls observed targeting org.freedesktop.DBus and org.mpris.MediaPlayer2.brave.instance479674.
bugs.location: voice_typing/daemon.py:1022-1023 (real ducker built on default config) and voice_typing/daemon.py:1804 (_arm → _duck_engage); test sites tests/test_key_listener.py:459-477, 483

bugs.title: bulk-text delivery fails its normative R.1 live-visibility requirement — words land at utterance granularity (up to 57-word backlog, sentence-end dumps) per the repo's own G5 gate
bugs.description: PRD §4.2sexies R.1 (normative, Rev 4): "Words MUST become visible in the focused editable field as recognition updates arrive — the operator reads the newest words at the insertion point while still speaking... never a sentence-end dump", and R.7 G5: "A sustained five-word backlog or a sentence-end dump fails regardless of medians." The shipped bulk-text path does not meet this: the repo's own timing gate (tests/G5_TIMING_EVIDENCE.md, 2026-11-23 @ c9a0a45) records BOTH routes as FAIL — im-gtk: one visible commit per replay (20 insertions / 0 corrections vs the ≥100/≥100 floors; 'the controller's per-utterance coalescing never let a partial op paint before its final superseded it'), sustained backlog max 57 words; pi-ghostty: speech→word-visible median 12,616 ms / p95 13,203 ms (bars: ≤500 ms / <1 s), sentence-end dump flagged, backlog max 57 words. A contributing cause is that only the laggy on_realtime_transcription_stabilized callback is wired as the partial source (voice_typing/daemon.py:221 _PARTIAL_CALLBACK_ATTR, with the in-code comment acknowledging the on_realtime_transcription_update fallback), while PRD R.8 explicitly prescribes comparing the earliest usable update callback against the stabilized one and choosing by VISIBLE word lag — that comparison was not performed. Net effect: with output.delivery="bulk-text", PRD acceptance #13's clause 'every recognition update is visible in the focused field' is not satisfied — dictation behaves like wait-for-silence delivery, exactly the experience the PRD's problem statement (§1) set out to eliminate. Mitigation context (why major, not critical): the mode is opt-in, G6 graduation honestly stayed opt-in (tests/G6_GRADUATION.md), and the failures are recorded rather than hidden; but the feature delivered for §4.2sexies does not conform to its own normative spec.
bugs.reproduction: Read tests/G5_TIMING_EVIDENCE.md (verdict table: im-gtk fail 'backlog sustained; counts 20/0 < 100'; pi-ghostty fail 'speech→visible 12.6 s median; backlog sustained; sentence-end dump'; thresholds-vs-measured table shows both routes breach 'sustained ≥5-word backlog must-not' with max 57 words). Re-run per the file's own commands: timeout -k 2 1500 env G5_TIMING_LAB=1 .venv/bin/python tests/g5_timing_lab.py --route im-gtk (and --route pi-ghostty with PI_BIN), each exits 1 with an honest-fail JSON verdict line. Static confirmation of the late partial source: voice_typing/daemon.py:219-221 wires only on_realtime_transcription_stabilized.
bugs.location: voice_typing/daemon.py:221 (_PARTIAL_CALLBACK_ATTR = on_realtime_transcription_stabilized) and voice_typing/bulk_controller.py (utterance-granularity delivery); evidence: tests/G5_TIMING_EVIDENCE.md

bugs.title: Permanently failing test: test_hypr_binds_use_portable_home_launcher rejects the documented SUPER+ALT+Escape panic bind
bugs.description: tests/test_systemd_unit.py::test_hypr_binds_use_portable_home_launcher asserts EVERY 'bind =' line in hypr-binds.conf contains '$HOME/.local/bin/voicectl' (VT-003 portability rule). The intentional panic bind added in commit 0e7dd05 ('bind = SUPER ALT, Escape, exec, systemctl --user stop voice-typing', hypr-binds.conf:60) deliberately bypasses voicectl and the control socket (PRD Rev 3(4): 'SUPER+ALT+Escape is a documented hard-kill panic bind'), so the test fails on every run. This is pre-existing at the delta base 2335a9e (bind landed 2026-10-25), but tests/test_systemd_unit.py was excluded from the G1 baseline ('not in the G1 set'), so — unlike the 16 documented legacy lazy-separator reds — this red is classified nowhere: the delta's final consistency sweep (P1.M7.T2.S3, 'confirm ... no unexplained new failures') left a permanently red, unexplained test in the suite. Either the test must exempt the documented panic bind or the bind line needs an exempting marker.
bugs.reproduction: cd /home/dustin/projects/voice-typing && timeout 120 .venv/bin/pytest tests/test_systemd_unit.py::test_hypr_binds_use_portable_home_launcher -q → fails with: AssertionError: hypr bind must use $HOME/.local/bin/voicectl (VT-003); got 'bind = SUPER ALT, Escape, exec, systemctl --user stop voice-typing' (tests/test_systemd_unit.py:336 vs hypr-binds.conf:60). Fails identically at the pre-delta base 2335a9e (verified via git show).

bugs.title: test_daemon.py misclassified as a CUDA hang vector and excluded from the G1 baseline — its 20 legacy-red tests were never classified
bugs.description: The G1 baseline (tests/G1_BASELINE.md) excluded tests/test_daemon.py as one of the 'contract-forbidden hang vectors' (grouped with test_feed_audio/test_recorder_host/test_cuda_check which do load real CUDA models). test_daemon.py is actually pure (its own header: 'NO real RealtimeSTT / NO model load / NO CUDA'; full run = 217 passed / 20 failed in ~16 s CPU-only). Its 20 failures are the same legacy lazy-separator contract class as the baseline's documented 16 (expected separator as a separate type op vs the lazy separator gluing it), but because the file was excluded they appear in no inventory. A delta-diff worktree comparison (base 2335a9e vs HEAD, same .venv) confirms the delta introduced ZERO new failures in this file and fixed one (test_status_snapshot_keys_and_cuda_values) — so this is documentation/classification debt, not a regression: the G1 'failure inventory' is incomplete, and any future sweep trusting 'test_daemon.py is a CUDA suite, don't run it' will keep flying blind over 20 reds. AGENTS.md's hang-vector table carries the same mislabel.
bugs.reproduction: cd /home/dustin/projects/voice-typing && timeout 500 .venv/bin/pytest tests/test_daemon.py -q --tb=no → 20 failed, 217 passed in ~16 s (no CUDA, no model load). git worktree add /tmp/vt-base 2335a9e && run the same file there with the repo .venv → 21 failed / 211 passed; the HEAD failure set is a strict subset of the base set (one fixed, zero new). Compare against tests/G1_BASELINE.md, which lists only 15 suites and excludes this file.
bugs.location: tests/G1_BASELINE.md (exclusion note) and AGENTS.md hang-vector table row 'uv run pytest ... test_daemon.py'; the unclassified reds live in tests/test_daemon.py (e.g. test_lost_sentinel_self_heals_after_timeout:5196)

summary: End-to-end PRD-validation hunt over the Rev-4 delta (D1 media ducking, D2 bulk-text delivery, D3 legacy defects) at HEAD 573d78f. Ran ~1,450 pure tests across 30+ suites: bulk contracts/controller/dispatch (126), ducking (69+31), IM transport/adapters (304), config/feedback/ctl/session (213), support labs (194), the G1 15-suite set, and the full test_daemon.py — plus direct behavioral probes (rendered_equal Unicode cases, session-recovery exclusion rules and the 1 MiB cap, config precondition triple, busctl side-effect proof, live voicectl CLI). Verified D3 closure landed (datagram merge + 6 ms contact gap + no-storm guard + hold-trace + suppression-chain bound all green), ducking sovereignty logic is correct (Stopped-vs-Paused restart hazard is guarded in the backend), session recovery matches R.6 exactly, G6/G3/README claims stay honestly labeled unverified, and a base-vs-HEAD worktree diff proves the delta introduced no regressions in the legacy suites (it fixed one). Four findings: (1) MAJOR, introduced by the duck_mode default flip — daemon-constructing tests fire real busctl --user calls against the live session, deterministically breaking later subprocess-recorder tests and able to pause the operator's playing media with no resume (R.7 violation); (2) MAJOR — the shipped bulk-text path fails its normative R.1 live-visibility requirement (both G5 routes: up to 57-word sustained backlog, sentence-end dumps, 12.6 s median speech→visible on pi-ghostty; only the laggy stabilized callback is wired despite R.8's mandate to compare callbacks) — honestly recorded in-repo and kept opt-in, but acceptance #13 is unmet; (3) MINOR — permanently red, unclassified VT-003 test vs the intentional panic bind; (4) MINOR — test_daemon.py is wrongly classified as a CUDA hang vector, leaving its 20 legacy reds outside the G1 inventory. The 16 documented legacy lazy-separator reds (test_streaming_commit/core/freeze) and the real-model watch set (test_streaming.py 3P/4F) reproduce exactly as baselined — pre-existing, classified, not re-filed. No daemon was foregrounded; the live systemd daemon was never armed by me; the base worktree and scratch files were removed.
recommendations: Make every daemon-constructing test hermetic: default cfg.audio.duck_mode='off' in shared fixtures (or inject a fake through the existing ducker= seam) and keep exactly one dedicated ducking-wiring test with a _FakeDucker — this removes both the order-dependent test pollution and the live-desktop side effect.

Pursue R.1/R.8 for bulk-text: wire the plain on_realtime_transcription_update callback (daemon.py:219 already documents the switch), re-run the G5 harness word-aligned, and re-evaluate whether partial ops can dispatch at update granularity ahead of their final.
Exempt the documented SUPER+ALT+Escape panic bind in test_hypr_binds_use_portable_home_launcher (or mark the line) so the suite carries no unexplained red.

Reclassify tests/test_daemon.py as a pure CPU suite in AGENTS.md and the G1 baseline, and fold its 20 legacy lazy-separator reds into the documented classification so future sweeps can diff against a complete inventory.
